verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents configurable session expiry (7-day default, `expiresIn`) and sliding refresh via `updateAge`, including a client-driven refresh flow. Its security docs also let a logged-in user revoke their own sessions on other devices. The evidence does not show immediate server-side or administrator revocation of a specific compromised session, nor how quickly a revoked session is invalidated. missing for 10: documented server-side/admin revocation of a specific compromised session, evidence that revocation takes effect immediately, independent or hands-on corroboration of the session lifecycle.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage session lifecycle — expiry, refresh, and immediate server-side revocation of a compromised session

citations.quote: The session expires after 7 days by default. But whenever the session is used and the updateAge is reached, the session expiration is updated
You can change both the `expiresIn` and `updateAge` values by passing the `session` object to the `auth` configuration.
The client automatically calls POST to perform the refresh.
A logged in user can also revoke their own sessions to log out from different devices or browsers.
